prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a parking lot collision in Sugar Land, Texas, and has concussion. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1348; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Can you confirm you're comfortable continuing?

A: Yes, that's fine.

Q: Please describe where you were when the collision happened.

A: I was in the parking lot of a shopping center in Sugar Land, Texas. I had just pulled into a space near the north entrance and was backing out to leave.

Q: What did you see as you were backing out?

A: Honestly, not much. There was a white SUV coming down the aisle, and I thought it was slowing down. I checked my mirror, but the angle was bad because of a column nearby.

Q: How fast were you moving when contact occurred?

A: Very slowly, maybe walking speed. But the impact was harder than I expected. My head snapped forward and then back against the headrest.

Q: Did you hit your head on anything?

A: I don't think so. It was more of a whiplash-type motion. But afterward I had a headache and felt dizzy, and the lights in the lot seemed too bright.

Q: Did you seek medical attention?

A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic that evening. They checked me out and said I had a concussion. They told me to rest and avoid screens for a while.

Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms?

A: Some. The headaches come and go, and I get tired faster than usual. I've had trouble concentrating at work, so I've been working reduced hours.

Q: Have you been seen by any other providers since?

A: I have a follow-up scheduled with my primary care doctor next week. I'm also keeping a log of my symptoms as the clinic suggested.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add?

A: Only that I want to make sure my vehicle damage and medical costs are documented properly. I've kept all my receipts and records.

Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.

A: Thank you.
